newsitem.title: USA: Oxford Health reports 77 percent rise in profits.
newsitem.headline: Oxford Health reports 77 percent rise in profits.

text.p: Oxford Health Plans Inc., a provider of medical plans in the Northeast, said a surge in enrollment and stable medical expenses buoyed earnings for the third quarter of 1996.
The Norwalk, Conn.-based company reported earnings of $26.65 million, or 33 cents a share in the third quarter, a 77 percent increase from $15.1 million, or 21 cents a share a year earlier.
Revenue rose 69 percent to $811.3 million from $480.2 million.
Meanwhile, enrollment in the health maintenance organisation's plans grew 57 percent to 1.44 million a the end of the third quarter and to about 1.5 million in November, the company said.

"Favorable medical cost trends and a continued reduction in the ratio of administrative expenses to operating revenues in the third quarter contributed to a 10 percent improvement in operating margins compared to the second quarter of 1996," said Chairman Stephen Wiggins.
Earnings for the first nine months of 1996 increased 84 percent to $67.6 million, or 86 cents per share, from $36.8 million, or 50 cents per share, for the first nine months of 1995.
Prior year per share amounts were restated to reflect a two-for-one stock split declared in March 1996.

Oxford's product lines include traditional health maintenance organisations, point-of-service plans, third-party administration of employer funded benefit plans, Medicare and Medicaid and dental plans.
The company markets its health plans to employers in New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut and New Hampshire.
